title: Perfect flat Cech model on a specified affine open
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be proper, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, with injective resolutions in $X.\mathrm{Modules}$, and let $F$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $f$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Fix an affine open $U$ of $T$ and derived localizations for $U$ and its localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. There exist a cochain complex $D$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and a natural $d$ such that $D$ is strictly zero outside $[0,d]$, every term is flat over the identity of $U$ and quasi-coherent, and its derived image is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. In every cartesian square $X'\to X$ over $T'\to U\to T$, with injective resolutions in $X'.\mathrm{Modules}$, $H^q(g^*D)$ is isomorphic to $R^qf'_*(g'^*F)$ for every natural $q$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. No termwise finite-presentation conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of f and compactness of the specified affine U make its inverse image compact. Take a finite subcover of its affine cover and reindex it by Fin r. Use the explicit finiteAffineCechModel of the restricted morphism and restricted coefficient. Its known bounds give strict degrees [0,r], and its terms are quasi-coherent. Relative flatness of the restricted module follows directly by applying hF to the images of affine opens under the two restriction open immersions, using morphismRestrict_appLE and ι_appIso to identify the scalar action. Apply finiteAffineCechModel_flatOver to obtain all termwise flatness statements.

Apply finiteAffineCechModel_perfect to this very affine cover and the original proper morphism and relatively flat finitely presented coefficient. This supplies only perfection of the fixed explicit complex, not the existence, boundedness, termwise flatness or the universal comparison clauses.

Apply finiteAffineCechModel_comparison to the same specified cover. It supplies the homology comparison for every base-change morphism and every supplied cartesian square, including nonaffine new bases. Assemble the explicit complex, the natural bound r, the two strict bounds, flatness, quasi-coherence, perfection and these comparison isomorphisms into the unchanged existential statement.
